guide.title: How to create an app password in Nextcloud
guide.step1: Open your Nextcloud and click your picture (top right) → Personal settings.
guide.step2: In the left menu, open Security.
guide.step3: Under "Devices & sessions", type a name (e.g. MyHomeLab backups) and click "Create new app password".
guide.step4: Copy the username and password shown and paste them here. The password is only shown once.
guide.generalOrPerService: You can have more than one destination (an app password, or even a Nextcloud user, for each) and choose in each MyHomeLab backup where it goes.
guide.safety: An app password only gives access to files and can be revoked in Nextcloud at any time without touching your password. MyHomeLab stores it encrypted and only deletes backups it created itself.

paperless.title: Paperless

connections.keySome_other: The user has {{count}} permissions. Calls without the permission show in red.

calls.noteAdd: Adds a note to a document
calls.bulkEdit: The same change on several documents

solidtime.title: solidtime
solidtime.description: Time tracking: the Timekeeper starts and stops the timer, logs forgotten hours, sums hours by project or client and organises projects.

solidtime.notFound: This solidtime does not exist or was disconnected.

solidtime.timerHint: The Timekeeper starts it when you ask.

connections.title: Connections

calls.objectUpdate: Changes a project, client, task or tag
calls.export: The organisation export (a zip with everything)
calls.import: Imports data from another service (Toggl, Clockify…)

stirling.title: Stirling-PDF
stirling.description: The PDF tools: the Archivist compresses, OCRs, merges, splits, rotates, converts, protects and signs PDFs from Paperless and Nextcloud, and looks after the Stirling settings.

stirling.notFound: This Stirling-PDF does not exist or was disconnected.

stirling.mcpHint_one: {{count}} tool; Claude Code connects to it
stirling.mcpHint_other: {{count}} tools; Claude Code connects to it
stirling.mcpOffHint: Turned on on the server (mcp.enabled); part of the paid Stirling
stirling.keyHint: What each access allows is in Connections.
stirling.notAdmin: The key is not an admin's: the Stirling-PDF settings cannot be read or changed with it (operations work).

connections.title: Connections
connections.permissionsAdmin: The key acts as the account that owns it. This one is an admin's: it runs every operation and reads and changes the server settings.
connections.permissionsNotAdmin: The key acts as the account that owns it. This one is not an admin's: operations work, the server settings do not.
connections.mcpOff: MCP: not on on this server.

allows.user: Every PDF operation, their list and the MCP

calls.endpoints: The operations disabled on the server

calls.mcp: The Stirling MCP (when it is on)
calls.releases: The published versions, with the notes
calls.pipeline: Runs several operations in a row (pipeline)

googleDrive.title: Google Drive
googleDrive.description: Your Drive and Google Sheets: Jarvis searches and reads everything and only changes what you link to a project.
googleDrive.meta: Reads all of Drive; only changes what is linked to a project.

links.title: Project links
links.description: Paste the link of a folder or a file and pick the project. Jarvis only changes what is here (and what is inside the folders); what it does with each file is in the project documents.
links.targetPlaceholder: Link of the folder or file in Drive
links.empty: Nothing linked yet: Jarvis can read, but changes nothing.
links.noProjects: Create a project in Projects first.

plane.title: Plane
plane.description: Project management: Jarvis sees the projects and work items, searches, and creates, changes and comments on work items in Plane.
plane.agentsNote: Jarvis uses Plane. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
plane.notFound: This Plane does not exist or was disconnected.
plane.accountDescription: The connection to Plane, with a personal token. Each connection is one workspace; the token acts as the user, with the role they have there.
plane.credentialsHint: The address, the workspace and the token. To change the token, connect again with a new one.
plane.mcpHint: Plane Community has no MCP on the server: Jarvis uses the MyHomeLab tools.

giteaMirror.title: Gitea Mirror
giteaMirror.description: GitHub mirrors in Gitea/Forgejo: the Infrastructure Engineer sees the status and failures, adds repositories and runs mirrors and syncs.
giteaMirror.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses Gitea Mirror. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
giteaMirror.notFound: This Gitea Mirror does not exist or was disconnected.
giteaMirror.accountDescription: The connection to Gitea Mirror, with an API key. A read-only key can look, but not mirror or add.
giteaMirror.credentialsHint: The address and the API key. To change the key, connect again with a new one.
giteaMirror.mcpHint: In Claude Code, Gitea Mirror’s own MCP is linked to the agent (needs version 3.46 or later).

jellyfin.title: Jellyfin
jellyfin.description: Movies, shows and music: Jarvis sees the libraries, searches, shows who is watching, manages users and tasks and scans for new files.
jellyfin.agentsNote: Jarvis uses Jellyfin. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
jellyfin.notFound: This Jellyfin does not exist or was disconnected.
jellyfin.accountDescription: The connection to Jellyfin, with an API key. The key gives admin access to the whole server.
jellyfin.credentialsHint: The address and the API key. To change the key, connect again with a new one.
jellyfin.pendingRestart: Jellyfin is waiting for a restart to apply changes (plugins or settings).

dispatcharr.title: Dispatcharr
dispatcharr.description: IPTV: Jarvis sees the channels, streams, M3U lists, EPG and who is watching, edits channels, refreshes the lists and schedules recordings.
dispatcharr.agentsNote: Jarvis uses Dispatcharr. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
dispatcharr.notFound: This Dispatcharr does not exist or was disconnected.
dispatcharr.accountDescription: The connection to Dispatcharr, with an admin's personal API key. The key acts as that user.
dispatcharr.credentialsHint: The address and the API key. To change the key, connect again with a new one.

coolify.title: Coolify
coolify.description: Where apps, services and databases run in Docker: the Infrastructure Engineer checks their state, deploys, starts and stops them, reads logs and changes variables.
coolify.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses Coolify. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
coolify.notFound: This Coolify does not exist or was already disconnected.
coolify.accountDescription: The connection to Coolify, with an API token. Agents can do what the token can: read to see, read:sensitive for logs and values, write and deploy to change and deploy.
coolify.credentialsHint: The address and API token. To change the token, connect again with a new one.
coolify.mcpHint: In Claude Code, Coolify's own MCP is attached to the agent. Turn it on in Coolify (for the instance and the token's team).

nginxProxyManager.title: Nginx Proxy Manager
nginxProxyManager.description: The proxy that puts apps on their domains, with SSL: the Infrastructure Engineer checks hosts and certificates, creates and changes proxy hosts and renews certificates.
nginxProxyManager.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses Nginx Proxy Manager. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
nginxProxyManager.notFound: This Nginx Proxy Manager does not exist or was already disconnected.
nginxProxyManager.accountDescription: The connection to Nginx Proxy Manager, with the email and password of a panel user (NPM has no API tokens). Agents can do what that user can.
nginxProxyManager.credentialsHint: The address, email and password. To change the password, disconnect and connect again.

tplinkRouter.title: TP-Link Archer
tplinkRouter.description: Your TP-Link router or extenders: the Infrastructure Engineer sees the Internet, the Wi-Fi and who is connected, and changes networks, IP reservations, ports and blocks when you ask.
tplinkRouter.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses the router and the extenders. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
tplinkRouter.notFound: This router or extender does not exist or was already disconnected.
tplinkRouter.accountDescription: The connection to the router's or extender's management page, with the user and the local password. It accepts one session at a time: MyHomeLab logs in only when needed and leaves after about 90 s idle.
tplinkRouter.credentialsHint: The address, the user and the local password. To change the password, disconnect and connect again.

stateHints.connected: MyHomeLab can log in to the management page.
stateHints.disconnected: The session dropped or the management page is busy. This is not an error: MyHomeLab tries again by itself.
stateHints.failed: The management page refused the password. Connect again with the right password.

connection.retryAt: I try again by myself every 5 minutes — next try at {{time}}.
connection.retrySoon: I try again by myself every 5 minutes.
connection.failedHint: I will not try this password again. Open the account, disconnect it and connect again with the right local password.
connection.reconnectHint: The saved password was refused. Disconnect this account and connect again with the local password (the TP-Link ID one does not work; on an EasyMesh extender it is usually the same as the main router).

overview.actionsNote: Renewing the IP cuts the Internet for a few seconds. Rebooting leaves the house without network for a few minutes.
overview.wanRenewQuestion: The Internet drops for a few seconds.
overview.rebootQuestion: The house is without network for a few minutes.
overview.actionsNoteExtender: Rebooting leaves everyone on the extender without network for a few minutes.
overview.rebootExtenderQuestion: Everyone on the extender loses the network for a few minutes.

wifi.none: The router did not show any Wi-Fi network.
wifi.turnOffQuestion: Everyone on this network loses Wi-Fi.

devices.search: Search by name, IP, MAC or extender
devices.blockHint: Blocking takes the device off the network. Unblock it in Access control.
devices.extenderHint: Blocks and IP reservations are done on the main router.

dhcp.noLeases: The router has no leases right now.
dhcp.extenderHint: An extender only shows the leases. Reservations are done on the main router.

ports.hint: Opening a port exposes that device to the Internet. Only open what you need.

access.title: Access control

modeHints.blacklist: Blocklist: everyone gets in except the blocked ones.
modeHints.whitelist: Allowlist: only devices on the list get in. Be careful not to lock yourself out.

access.unavailable: This router does not show access control.

kindHints.router: The main router: it has the Internet, DHCP, ports and access control.
kindHints.extender: An extender: it repeats the main router's Wi-Fi. Blocks, IP reservations and ports are done on the router.

backhaul.title: Link to the main router
backhaul.unknown: The extender did not show its link to the router.

clickhouse.title: ClickHouse
clickhouse.description: Analytics database: Jarvis sees the databases, tables and queries, runs read queries and, when you ask, write SQL on ClickHouse.
clickhouse.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses ClickHouse. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
clickhouse.notFound: This ClickHouse does not exist or was disconnected.
clickhouse.accountDescription: The connection to ClickHouse over the HTTP interface, with a user and password. Agents can do whatever that user can: to only read, use a readonly user.
clickhouse.credentialsHint: The address, the user and the password. To change the password, connect again with the new one.
clickhouse.notAdmin: This user cannot see users and grants (SHOW ACCESS).

postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Database: Jarvis sees the databases, tables, connections and maintenance, runs read queries and, when you ask, write SQL on PostgreSQL.
postgres.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses PostgreSQL. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
postgres.notFound: This PostgreSQL does not exist or was disconnected.
postgres.accountDescription: A direct connection to the PostgreSQL server (host and port), with a user and password. Agents can do whatever that user can: to only read, use a user with pg_read_all_data.
postgres.credentialsHint: The host, port, database, user, password and SSL. To change the password, connect again with the new one.
postgres.notSuperuser: This user is not a superuser: it only sees its own connections and queries and cannot stop others' (unless it has pg_monitor and pg_signal_backend).

vaultwarden.title: Vaultwarden
vaultwarden.description: The password vault (Bitwarden compatible): the Infrastructure Engineer sees the users, 2FA and settings, invites people and disables accounts. The vaults stay encrypted: nobody reads them.
vaultwarden.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses Vaultwarden. For another agent, choose its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
vaultwarden.notFound: This Vaultwarden does not exist or was disconnected.
vaultwarden.accountDescription: The connection to the Vaultwarden admin panel, with the ADMIN_TOKEN. It manages users and shows the settings; the passwords stored in the vaults are encrypted and cannot be read.
vaultwarden.credentialsHint: The address and the admin token. To change the token, connect again with the new one.
vaultwarden.twoFactorHint: People with an account who have not turned on two-step login yet.
vaultwarden.vaultNote: The vaults are encrypted with each person's master password: MyHomeLab never asks for it nor reads the stored passwords.

infisical.title: Infisical
infisical.description: The secrets manager: the Infrastructure Engineer sees the projects, environments and secrets, and creates and changes secrets and folders when you ask.
infisical.agentsNote: The Infrastructure Engineer uses Infisical. For another agent, choose its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
infisical.notFound: This Infisical does not exist or was disconnected.
infisical.accountDescription: The connection to Infisical with a Machine Identity (Universal Auth). Agents only see the projects the identity was added to, and only do what its role allows.
infisical.credentialsHint: The address, the Client ID and the Client Secret. To change the secret, connect again with the same Client ID.
infisical.environmentsHint: Adding up the environments of every project the identity sees.
infisical.updateHint: Infisical does not report the installed version through the API: it only says when a newer one exists.
infisical.noProjects: The identity sees no project: add it to a project in Access Control → Machine Identities.
infisical.identityNote: To read and write secrets, the identity needs a role with those permissions in each project (e.g. Developer or Admin).

forgejoModal.title: Connect Forgejo
forgejoModal.name: Name (optional)
forgejoModal.tokenHint: In Forgejo: Settings → Applications → Generate token, with read and write on "repository" and "issue", and read on "user". To back up the whole instance, use an administrator account and also give read on "admin".

trekModal.title: Connect TREK
trekModal.name: Name (optional)
trekModal.hint: Use an administrator account without MFA (MyHomeLab has no way to give the code). The password is stored encrypted.
trekModal.mcpHint: So agents get the whole TREK API: in TREK, Settings → Integrations → MCP → New Client → "Machine client". It can also be connected later, on the TREK page.

homeAssistantModal.title: Connect Home Assistant
homeAssistantModal.name: Name (optional)
homeAssistantModal.hint: In Home Assistant: your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. It must belong to an administrator. The token is stored encrypted.

adguardModal.title: Connect AdGuard
adguardModal.name: Name (optional)
adguardModal.hint: The username and password you use for the AdGuard Home dashboard (AdGuard has no tokens). The password is stored encrypted.

openGymModal.title: Connect openGym
openGymModal.name: Name (optional)
openGymModal.codeHint: In openGym: Settings → pair the phone app → it shows an 8-letter code. Paste it here within 5 minutes (it works once). MyHomeLab connects like the phone app.

gameTrackerModal.title: Connect GamesTracker
gameTrackerModal.name: Name (optional)
gameTrackerModal.tokenHint: In GamesTracker: Settings → API → New token. For agents to change the shelf, do not make it read-only. Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

immichModal.title: Connect Immich
immichModal.name: Name (optional)
immichModal.apiKeyHint: In Immich: Account (your avatar) → Account settings → API keys → New API key. For agents to change settings, jobs and backups, create it in an admin account with the "all" permission. Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

paperlessModal.title: Connect Paperless
paperlessModal.name: Name (optional)
paperlessModal.tokenHint: In Paperless: your profile (top right) → My Profile → API Auth Token → generate. For agents to change the configuration, use a superuser's. Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

solidtimeModal.title: Connect solidtime
solidtimeModal.name: Name (optional)
solidtimeModal.tokenHint: In solidtime: your profile → API Tokens → Create token. Copy all of it (it is long). Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.
solidtimeModal.organizationHint: Only if you are in more than one: the name of the one to connect. For another, connect again.

cronJobs.title: Cron jobs
cronJobs.description: Tasks MyHomeLab runs on its own, in code and without AI, at the interval you choose.
cronJobs.adguardNote: Turning one of these on sets AdGuard's own list interval to "never", so the lists are not updated twice.
cronJobs.empty: This app has no cron jobs yet.

adguard_refresh_blocklists.title: Update the blocklists
adguard_refresh_blocklists.description: Downloads AdGuard's blocked DNS lists and says how many changed.

adguard_refresh_allowlists.title: Update the allowlists
adguard_refresh_allowlists.description: Downloads AdGuard's allowed domain lists and says how many changed.

proxmox_disk_alert.title: Disk almost full alert
proxmox_disk_alert.description: Checks the disk of each CT and VM; above the limit it alerts and, if you want, the agent handles it on the board.

updates_app.title: App updates
updates_app.description: Checks for a new version of the app and, if you want, puts it on the board right away, in the column you choose.

updates_ha_components.title: Add-on, HACS and firmware updates
updates_ha_components.description: Checks for new versions of the Home Assistant components and, if you want, puts each one on the board right away.

updates_nextcloud_apps.title: Nextcloud app updates
updates_nextcloud_apps.description: Checks for new versions of the apps installed in Nextcloud and, if you want, puts each one on the board right away.

cronJobs.proxmoxNote: The agent only steps in when an alert asks for it.

diskAlert.agent: The agent picks it up, studies and fixes it
diskAlert.agentHint: Each alert becomes a task on the server board (Projects): the agent studies what uses the space and, within the limits below, cleans what is safe or grows a CT disk; for anything else it asks you (Waiting for reply).
diskAlert.limitsNote: On a VM the agent always asks before growing. The storage free minimum always applies, even when you approve.
diskAlert.noAgent: Without the QEMU guest agent, the disk inside is unknown for: {{guests}}. Install qemu-guest-agent in the VM and enable it in Options → QEMU Guest Agent.

updates.boardHint: Each new version becomes a board task right away. Without this it just stays available, waiting for an agent.

columnHint.new: It stays in Todo until you drag it to Waiting for study.
columnHint.study: The study starts on its own and follows the usual path: it only installs with your yes, as the app rules say.

stirlingModal.title: Connect Stirling-PDF
stirlingModal.name: Name (optional)
stirlingModal.apiKeyHint: In Stirling-PDF: Account settings → API key → show or generate (login must be on). For the agents to change the settings, use an admin's. It is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

planeModal.title: Connect Plane
planeModal.name: Name (optional)
planeModal.workspaceHint: What comes right after the address in a Plane link (https://plane.example.com/my-team/…). You can paste the link.
planeModal.apiKeyHint: In Plane: Profile settings → Personal Access Tokens → Add personal access token. Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

giteaMirrorModal.title: Connect Gitea Mirror
giteaMirrorModal.name: Name (optional)
giteaMirrorModal.apiKeyHint: In Gitea Mirror: Configuration → Authentication → API Keys → Create (full access to mirror; read only to look). Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

jellyfinModal.title: Connect Jellyfin
jellyfinModal.name: Name (optional)
jellyfinModal.apiKeyHint: In Jellyfin: Dashboard → API Keys → + (name it MyHomeLab). It is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

dispatcharrModal.title: Connect Dispatcharr
dispatcharrModal.name: Name (optional)
dispatcharrModal.apiKeyHint: In Dispatcharr (v0.20 or newer): Users → your admin → API & XC tab → Generate. It is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

coolifyModal.title: Connect Coolify
coolifyModal.name: Name (optional)
coolifyModal.apiTokenHint: In Coolify: Keys & Tokens → API tokens → Create (grant read, read:sensitive, write and deploy). The API must be enabled in Settings → Advanced. It is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

nginxProxyManagerModal.title: Connect Nginx Proxy Manager
nginxProxyManagerModal.name: Name (optional)
nginxProxyManagerModal.urlHint: The address where you open the panel (usually port 81; plain http on the local network is fine).
nginxProxyManagerModal.hint: A panel user without two-factor login (ideally one just for MyHomeLab). The password is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

tplinkRouterModal.title: Connect TP-Link Archer
tplinkRouterModal.name: Name (optional)

clickhouseModal.title: Connect ClickHouse

postgresModal.title: Connect PostgreSQL
postgresModal.name: Name (optional)

postgresModal.passwordHint: Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab, never in the address.

vaultwardenModal.title: Connect Vaultwarden
vaultwardenModal.name: Name (optional)
vaultwardenModal.adminTokenHint: The server's ADMIN_TOKEN, in plain text: what you type to enter /admin (not the argon2 hash). Without it set, the panel is off. It is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.

infisicalModal.title: Connect Infisical
infisicalModal.name: Name (optional)
infisicalModal.identityHint: In Infisical: Organization → Access Control → Identities → Create Identity, Universal Auth method → Create Client Secret. Then add the identity to the projects (Access Control → Machine Identities). The secret is stored encrypted in MyHomeLab.
